Posted February 18, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan

The story below is doubly sad.

First, it drags the Voice of America, which was once intended to be a source of truth and freedom down into the sewer of prohibitionist propaganda. Of course many other DEAland agencies have been subverted.
See
Add The Agriculture Department To The Institutions Corrupted By Marijuana Prohibition. -- 2 Articles
Second, it demonstrates one more example of Canadian prohibitionists putting their ideology ahead of their country's freedom and sovereignty, but not for the first time.
See
Documenting The Role of Politicized Canadian Police In Maintaining Cannabis Prohibition. Canadian Narks Versus Canadian Freedom. Following the DEA Party Line. The Battle for Canada
and
Canada Exports A Little Reefer to DEAland. Imports A Lot of Reefer Madness. A Bad Balance of Trade. Canadian Taxpayers Are Being Lied to At Their Own Expense, But It May Also Cost Them Their Freedom.
and
Canadian Police Association Demonstrates The Role of Ideology in the Maintenance of Marijuana Prohibition. Sweden Ideal While the Dutch Are the Worst. Analysis by Richard Cowan.

The VOA story relies on two BC prohibitionists who have a public record that could easily have been checked, for example on MarijuanaNews. Corporal Scott Rintoul is with the Drug Awareness Section of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Vancouver, and has a long history of lying to the DEAland media.
See
Someone Floats A Rumor That DEAland Wants To Blacklist Canada;
Washington Denies Everything, But Canadian Prohibitionists Seem To Cheer,
Sort Of 3 Articles
and
The Toronto Star Carries A Good " Business " Story On British Columbian Marijuana Industry
and
" Enforcers Challenge Cannabis Liberation Movement " In Canada Great Journalism!!!
The Globe and Mail Canada's National Newspaper

The VOA article also tells us that its other source, Criminology professor Darryl Plecas, of the University College of the Fraser Valley near Vancouver, has studied the marijuana trade for years. Yes, and he continues to be either incompetent or dishonest, or both.
See
The Agenda for the Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
The Prohibitionist Counterattack In Canada Runs Into Some Flack. RCMP Challenged. And I Have Fun Writing A Letter to the Editor. The thrust of the article is that BC Bud is smuggled to DEAland and traded for cocaine, guns, methamphetamines, and everything bad that any of them can think of, which is then smuggled back into Canada. At least they do not repeat the canard about it being traded " pound for pound. "
See
How the Canadian Prohibitionists Equate Marijuana And Cocaine In the New Party Line

Of course, to whatever degree this claim might be true, and no supporting evidence is offered, then it would be just one more argument for the legalization of cannabis to take it out of the distribution channels with other contraband. The separation of the markets for cannabis and other drugs is the foundation of all Dutch drugs policies.
See
 " The failure of Dutch drug policy " An Examination of Prohibitionist Propaganda and the Official Dutch Government Response -- Special To MarijuanaNews

I gather that this sort of barter actually does take place, but there is no indication from the official data that it is a common practice, but the VOA story implies that it is standard: The illicit plant is being traded not for cash, but cocaine.

It is indeed sad that the Voice of America has traded its integrity for cannabis prohibition.

From The Voice of America:
Canada Launches Effort to Halt Marijuana for Cocaine Trade
By Craig McCulloch
Vancouver
February 13, 2004
(Also available in audio at the above link.)

Illegal marijuana crops worth billions of dollars each year are flourishing
in the Canadian province of British Columbia. Both Canadian and American
authorities are now making large seizures of not only drugs, but also weapons, houses and boats.
(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, RCMP seizures of BC Bud remained essentially unchanged from 1998 to 2002, the last year for which numbers are available at around 3.5 million grams.

On the other hand, the total amount of cannabis seized in Canada, nationwide, in 2002 increased to 54 million from 30 million grams in 1998.

Now take a look at those numbers.

That's right. Seizures in BC were less than seven percent of all cannabis seizures in Canada!

In 2002, Ontario accounted for over 16 million grams, and Quebec accounted for over 30 million grams, roughly ten times the seizures in BC.
From Marihuana Cultivation in Canada: Evolution and Current Trends - November 2002:

The illicit plant is being traded not for cash, but cocaine.
(MarijuanaNews note: Taken literally, that sentence would mean that all or certainly most of the BC Bud is bartered. Of course, there is not the slightest evidence to support such an idea.)

Marijuana growing in British Columbia is estimated to be worth billions of dollars a year. It is one of the province's major illegal exports. In most cases, the high-grade drug is being sent southward into the United States, exchanged directly for cocaine that has made its way through U.S. territory to the Canadian border.
(MarijuanaNews note: Now we are being told most of the BC Bud is going South to be traded for cocaine! Of course, once again there is absolutely no data to support this claim.)

Canada is now the second highest source of marijuana in the United States.
See
As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That
(MarijuanaNews note: In 2003 the U.S. Customs and Border Patrol made 17,716 marijuana seizures of 2.1 million pounds at the Mexican border, but only 20,000 pounds were seized at the Canadian border. Moreover, the RCMP says,The U.S. are basically their own main source of marihuana.

According to the Drug Czar's website, in 2001 Mexico accounted for 7,400 metric tons (one million grams per metric ton) of the world total of 14,900 metric tons. The only other country that is listed separately is Colombia with 4,000 metric tons. The rest of the world combined only produces 3,500 metric tons. But notice that they say nothing about DEAland's own production.)

The RCMP says, Based on the seizures and average yield per plant, the current [Canadian] annual production is estimated to be about 800 tonnes.


While fighting the illegal trade, Canadian authorities have recently been making large seizures. During a series of raids on one day late last year, Canadian police agencies confiscated one Cessna aircraft, three boats, 22 different types of weapons including two machine guns, 3,300 marijuana plants, and replica police jackets.
(MarijuanaNews note: Yes, but was that typical? No, it wasn't.)
Just this past week, police raided six high end homes in a Vancouver suburb and confiscated 4,000 plants. Police are planning on confiscating two of the houses if they can prove the owners were the marijuana farmers.

Scott Rintoul
Corporal Scott Rintoul is with the Drug Awareness Section of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Vancouver. He says weapons, cocaine, and other drugs started being used as currency in exchange for marijuana because of changes to banking laws.

" There were some restrictions put on by the federal government and provincial government on how much you could transfer and how much money you could change, " he said. " So it became very disruptive and it was a challenge to change money. Almost overnight, they realize that they can actually just take marijuana across the border and trade that for cocaine. And that started about 1995 and that continues today. And that's sort of the big trade now is marijuana being traded for guns, for cocaine, for methamphetamine, which then comes back into Canada. "

Darryl Plecas
The Organized Crime Agency in Vancouver estimates there are currently 10,000 commercial growing operations throughout the province. Each location contains an average of 400 plants that provides three or four harvests every year, which earns the grower over $1 million. On the streets of Los Angeles, the drug gets $5,000 for about one half of a kilogram and as much as $8,000 in eastern cities like New York.

Criminology professor Darryl Plecas, of the University College of the Fraser Valley near Vancouver, has studied the marijuana trade for years.

He says trading marijuana for cocaine is lowering the cash cost to bring large amounts of cocaine into Canada. This is worsening an already dangerous trade.
(MarijuanaNews note: Cocaine seizures in Canada have not increased over the last few years, so there is no evidence for this claim.)

" If I want to purchase a huge amount of cocaine, now that I have marijuana, I don't need the same amount of money, " said Darryl Plecas. " I just need to get my hands on enough marijuana, which matches what they're asking for in cocaine and away I go. So, all of sudden you in effect reduce your cost of cocaine to buy it for trafficking purposes to a very small amount. This [is a] very dangerous situation. "
(MarijuanaNews note: I have a longstanding interest in the economics of contraband.
See
How The Narcs Created Crack By Richard C. Cowan

So, I have really tried to figure out how this might work. Suppose that Liberal Party fundraisers smuggle BC Bud to DEAland, and they decide to trade it for cocaine.

This would theoretically work best in the Los Angeles area where BC Bud, if it is really good, will presumably sell for the highest price, and cocaine would sell for the lowest price, being close to the Mexican point of entry to DEAland for the coke.

The reason that BC would bring a higher price in LA is that there is a risk premium on bringing it so far south, and there are people there who will pay more for the best even though they really have no way of knowing where the kind bud really originated. BC Bud is not distinguishable from other weed. It looks the same as Humboldt indoor or outdoor.

In any case, the cocaine will now have to be smuggled north through DEAland and then across the Canadian border. This scenario seems rather inherently improbable. That may be why the 2002RCMP reportdoes not mention a single large cocaine seizure from the US.)

Ken Peterson
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency opened a Vancouver office in June of last year. The Resident Agent in Charge, Ken Peterson says the size of the marijuana trade is getting the agency's attention. He says the new trade of exchanging marijuana for cocaine has resulted in a significant increase of trafficking and as a result, arrests and seizures.
See
The Drug Czar Harvests BC Bud Propaganda Campaign At Canadian Border. The Jails Are Full, But He Likes That.

" Oh it's a major concern. The BC [British Columbia] bud - Canada and especially western Canada is a source country for the BC bud, " said Mr. Peterson. " The United States gets their cocaine both from Central and South America. The free flow and the larger seizures of cocaine being seized both at the American and the Canadian side of the border has increased significantly lately as the marijuana coming south into the United States. The seizures and the intelligence has also increased significantly recently. "

To help this growing battle against the marijuana and cocaine trade, the new Canadian government of Prime Minister Paul Martin will soon reintroduce legislation to deal with the marijuana issue.
See
The Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Escalates. Blatant Drive to Create DEAland Style Police State. Phony Decrim Bill Gets Even Worse.
